description: Data layer harness (DAT-01): audit repros and critic predictions against today's stack on SQLite, MariaDB and PostgreSQL, from core/test/database/regressions and packages/database/test/regressions. Server-scoped entries apply to the database suite's legs; DAT-02..DAT-15 empty it.

test: writes inside a transaction roll back with it
a write through dataSource.getRepository inside transaction()

failure.message: ^the repository write committed on another connection and survived the rollback
failure.name: AssertionError

entries.reason: Audit: withRollback/loadFixtures do not roll back writes made through dataSource.getRepository on server drivers. The old stack's transaction() (core/src/database/transaction.ts) keeps its manager in AsyncLocalStorage and only ApplicationRecord.getRepository reads it, so a write through the data source takes another pooled connection, commits on its own and survives the rollback (sql.js joins through the connection lease, so SQLite passes). DAT-04 binds the new stack's transactions at the engine lease (packages/database/test/conformance/transaction proves every lease taken inside a transaction joins it on all three drivers); this repro of the old stack goes when DAT-15b deletes core/src/database.

test: writes inside a transaction roll back with it
a write through dataSource.getRepository inside withRollback

failure.message: ^withRollback left the repository write behind for the next test
failure.name: AssertionError

entries.reason: Audit: withRollback/loadFixtures do not roll back writes made through dataSource.getRepository on server drivers. The old stack's withRollback (core/src/database/testing/test-database.ts) rides transaction(), which keeps its manager in AsyncLocalStorage that only ApplicationRecord.getRepository reads, so a write through the data source takes another pooled connection, commits on its own and survives the rollback (sql.js joins through the connection lease, so SQLite passes). DAT-12's withTestTransaction binds at the engine lease, and packages/database/test/testing/rollback-coverage.database.test.ts proves every write path (record pipeline, set writes, link tables, model-set handles, raw SQL, fixtures, factories, seeders) leaves no row behind on all three drivers; this repro of the old stack goes when DAT-15b deletes core/src/database.

test: writes inside a transaction roll back with it
fixtures loaded inside withRollback

failure.message: ^withRollback left the fixture rows behind
failure.name: AssertionError

entries.reason: Audit: withRollback/loadFixtures do not roll back writes made through dataSource.getRepository on server drivers. The old stack's loadFixtures saves through dataSource.getRepository (core/src/database/fixtures.ts), and its withRollback rides transaction(), whose manager only ApplicationRecord.getRepository reads, so the fixture rows commit on another pooled connection and survive the rollback (sql.js joins through the connection lease, so SQLite passes). DAT-12's loadFixtures writes through the bound data source's engine lease, and packages/database/test/testing/rollback-coverage.database.test.ts proves fixtures loaded inside withTestTransaction leave no row behind on all three drivers; this repro of the old stack goes when DAT-15b deletes core/src/database.

test: live change capture of set-form writes
Model.update(criteria, set) is captured

failure.message: ^the committed update reached no live subscriber
failure.name: AssertionError

entries.reason: Critic prediction: live capture silently drops set-form writes. The capture reads the primary key off the event entity, and a query-builder UPDATE carries only the SET map, outside any transaction frame (core/src/live/change-capture.ts), so no change record is emitted. The new stack's change feed reports set writes (@jsails/database, packages/database/test/record/change-feed.database.test.ts); this old-stack capture keeps the defect until core/src/database and its capture are deleted.

test: a model with a datetime column
builds its metadata and table on this driver

failure.message: ^Data type "datetime" in "Appointment\.starts_at" is not supported by "postgres" database\.$

entries.reason: Audit: every app model with a Date field fails on Postgres. ModelColumnType names the MySQL/SQLite type 'datetime' and defineModel lowers it verbatim before the driver is known; TypeORM's postgres driver rejects it.

test: a model with a datetime column
reads back the Date it wrote, to the millisecond

failure.message: ^(?:the Date came back as 2026-03-04T05:06:07\.000Z, not 2026-03-04T05:06:07\.089Z(?:\n|$)|Data type "datetime" in "Appointment\.starts_at" is not supported by "postgres" database\.)

entries.reason: DAT-03 fidelity rule (millisecond timestamps). MariaDB: 'datetime' lowers to DATETIME with no fractional precision, so the milliseconds are dropped; the message pins exactly that value, so any other change (a timezone shift) fails as unexpected. PostgreSQL: the model cannot be built at all ('datetime' is not a postgres type).

test: foreign key columns are indexed
a many-to-one join column has an index after the schema push

failure.message: ^regression_books\.author_id has no index
failure.name: AssertionError

entries.reason: Audit: defineModel creates foreign keys without an index on the join column (Postgres and SQLite). A many-to-one lowers to ManyToOne + JoinColumn with no index; MariaDB passes only because InnoDB indexes every foreign key itself.

test: db:push after a plugin is removed from plugins.use
a push with nothing destructive of the app's own is not blocked

failure.message: ^the removed plugin's table blocked a push that changes nothing
failure.name: AssertionError

entries.reason: Audit: the db:push destructive gate is all-or-nothing and one stray table blocks every safe change. A JsailsDataSource database config, which every starter writes, still pushes through planSchema in core/src/cli/commands/db-schema.ts, which diffs against the declared models only, so the removed plugin's table is a planned drop and the whole push needs --allow-destructive. The schema core (packages/database/src/schema) approves operations one by one but is reached only by a defineSchemaConfig() config until app models and the starters move onto it.

test: db:push after a plugin is removed from plugins.use
--allow-destructive does not drop the removed plugin's table

failure.message: ^the app's push dropped the removed plugin's table and its data
failure.name: AssertionError

entries.reason: Critic prediction: removing a plugin from plugins.use turns its tables into drops, and one --allow-destructive authorises them. The app's push has no record of who owns a table (planSchema in core/src/cli/commands/db-schema.ts always plans with allowDestructive: true).

test: statement budgets
loading a has-many relation for many parents costs one statement for the children

failure.message: ^expected 2 SELECTs \(the parents, then their replies\), got 3:\n
failure.name: AssertionError

entries.reason: Audit: eager loading runs two queries per relation. The loader selects (pk, fk) pairs and then re-selects the same children by primary key, because the hydrated child does not carry its foreign key (core/src/database/relation-loader/loaders.ts). Today's count, 3, is pinned in the message, so a worse count fails as unexpected. DAT-09 loads each relation level with one statement whose rows carry their foreign key (packages/database/src/relation; packages/database/test/conformance/relation/load-plan.database.test.ts counts 100 parents with 200 children each at 2 statements on all three drivers); this repro of the old stack goes when DAT-15b deletes core/src/database.

test: statement budgets
saving a loaded, modified record sends no SELECT

failure.message: ^expected no SELECT before the UPDATE, got 1:\n
failure.name: AssertionError

entries.reason: Critic prediction: save() on a loaded record pays a SELECT before every UPDATE; TypeORM's SubjectExecutor reloads the row to diff it. Today's count, 1, is pinned in the message, so a second SELECT fails as unexpected. The new stack's save sends the UPDATE alone (packages/database/test/record/pipeline.database.test.ts); the old stack keeps the defect until core/src/database is deleted.

test: package stores inside a test transaction
a flag set inside withTestTransaction is rolled back with it

failure.message: ^(?:the flag write survived the rollback of its test transaction(?:\n|$)|Data type "datetime" in "JsailsFeatureFlag\.updatedAt" is not supported by "postgres" database\.$)

entries.reason: Critic prediction: framework stores that capture a repository from the data source do not join an ambient transaction. On MariaDB the flags store's write takes its own pooled connection and commits, so it survives withTestTransaction's rollback (the assertion). On PostgreSQL the store fails before that point: its entity declares 'datetime'. Once that is fixed the PostgreSQL branch becomes the same rollback assertion, which stays failing until DAT-13 ports the store onto the new stack, whose transactions DAT-04 binds at the engine lease.

test: portable type fidelity
json
round-trips, orders and compares as the application does

failure.message: ^the database returned a value the column type does not write \(v: json\)
failure.name: ColumnValueError

entries.reason: The engine breaks its own contract that JSON comes back as the server's text: MariaDB marks a json_valid-checked LONGTEXT as JSON in its extended metadata and mysql2 parses it unless the connection sets jsonStrings, so a stored JSON string value cannot be told from text.
